title: John Chrysostom on Ezekiel 3:1
body: “Surely these things were said for their sakes, that they might have no pretense of excuse. Since if this were not the case, what shall He have more than Isaiah?”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on John and Hebrews

title: John Chrysostom on Ezekiel 3:15
body: “But if they be themselves dumb, how did they give responses to others? And wherefore did the demon lead them to the images?”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on the Epistles to the Corinthians

title: John Chrysostom on Ezekiel 3:19
body: “These things I have said, not as dictating to you, but only to secure and protect you. Since every one of you is come to age, and will have to give account of the things which he has done, I entreat you not to cast the whole matter on us, and consider yourselves to be irresponsible, that ye may not go on fruitlessly deceiving yourselves, and at last bewail it.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Galatians through Philemon

title: John Chrysostom on Ezekiel 3:19
body: “I could have wished to know for certain whether any hear with fitting earnestness the things that are said, whether we are not casting the seeds by the wayside: for in that case I should have made my instructions with more cheerfulness. For we shall speak, though no one hear, for the fear which is laid on us by our Saviour.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on John and Hebrews

title: John Chrysostom on Ezekiel 9:8
body: “What then," saith one, "if they be enemies and heathens, must one hate them?" One must hate, not them but their doctrine: not the man, but the wicked conduct, the corrupt mind.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on the Epistles to the Corinthians

title: John Chrysostom on Ezekiel 9:11
body: “Moral. Let not any one of them that eat this Passover look towards Egypt, but towards Heaven, towards "Jerusalem that is above." (Gal.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Galatians through Philemon

title: John Chrysostom on Ezekiel 13:19
body: “There were, it is likely, in the time of our forefathers also, some who "weakened the hands of the people" (Jer.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Galatians through Philemon

title: John Chrysostom on Ezekiel 16:21
body: “And if it be given her for a covering," say you, "wherefore need she add another covering?" That not nature only, but also her own will may have part in her acknowledgment of subjection.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on the Epistles to the Corinthians
